part_name: AM59 Sealed Mast Head V2 - Structural Load-Bypass Frame
assumptions: The primary release-gated body is the continuously connected structural frame, including its 605 mm asymmetric longitudinal cradle rails that reach beneath the external wet bay. Each upper/lower interface is a 250 mm central blank plate with connected post landing pads rather than a mass-heavy full rectangular sheet. The enclosure, lid, gasket, cartridge, heat exchangers, fans, and references are separately fabricated or procured assembly items.
The AM59 STEP is placed with its mounting plane at Z=52 mm, fan inlet toward -X, and RF output toward +X. The transform is fixed from the supplied vendor geometry.
The structural frame bypasses all antenna and rotator loads around the sealed electronics enclosure.
The dry enclosure is a continuously welded body with a single gasketed -X service opening. Its declared 600 x 270 x 260 mm envelope excludes removable exterior accessories.
The wet-side cooling module may flood during temporary immersion but no wet-side air or drain path crosses the continuous thermal bulkhead into the dry chamber.
IP66/IP67 and any NEMA claims describe qualification targets only until the fully assembled unit, with every connector mated or capped, passes the applicable third-party tests.
A max_interference allowance of 0.5 mm^3 tolerates coincident contact faces and STEP-kernel noise, not physical component overlap.
unresolved: Existing lower plate and rotator interface patterns, materials, fasteners, datums, and allowable moments require physical survey and structural substantiation before fabrication.
The thermal module must demonstrate at least the project-specified dry-side-to-ambient conductance on the final system curve; its fin geometry is not released by this envelope model.
Final RF, power, and control bulkheads require documented mated and capped IP67 performance plus electrical, RF peak-power, creepage, and corrosion qualification.
Gasket compound, vent membrane, coatings, and galvanic isolation must be selected against the actual washdown chemicals, salt exposure, UV dose, and temperature range.
Combined enclosure, rotator, horn, cable, wind, transport-shock, and overturning loads remain to be checked against the BlueSky mast configuration and guying limits.
